canonical_topic: Why natural gas is transported by pipeline rather than pressurized containers
definition: Methane's low energy density per unit volume, relative to heavier hydrocarbons, makes pipeline transport the practical choice over pressurized container shipping.
core_idea: Because methane holds relatively little heat energy per unit of volume compared to longer-chain hydrocarbons like propane or butane, moving it in pressurized metal containers would require impractically large containers, so pipelines are used instead.
key_points: Propane and butane contain enough energy density to be practically shipped in pressurized metal containers
Methane requires a much larger container to hold an equivalent amount of heat energy, making container transport impractical at scale
Pipelines solve this by allowing continuous transport without needing to contain large volumes under pressure in discrete vessels
relationships: Low energy density of methane -> reliance on pipeline infrastructure rather than tanker/cylinder transport
trading_implications: Regions without pipeline access to a given supply source face a structurally different (and often costlier) transport option: liquefaction/LNG shipping
caveats: Assuming natural gas could be economically shipped in pressurized tanks the way propane or butane are
